Proffit · Classifications & Indices

Every way orthodontics sorts the world into categories — classifications, treatment-need indices, and maturity/staging systems — with the schematic from the book. Proffit 7th ed.

Pairs with — Ceph Norms → Important Numbers →

Classification systems 6

Angle classification 16

Based on the first-molar relationship & the line of occlusion: Class I (normal molar), Class II div 1 (proclined) / div 2 (retroclined), Class III. Subdivisions = unilateral.

Ackerman-Proffit 6

Five-characteristics Venn that fixes Angle's gaps — adds crowding/symmetry, profile, and the three spatial planes to the AP molar reading.

Rotational classification 6

The dentition can also translate in 3-D and rotate about three axes — pitch (up/down), roll (canting), yaw (one side forward → midline + asymmetric class).

Andrews' six keys 610

Keys to normal occlusion: (1) molar relationship, (2) crown angulation/tip, (3) crown inclination/torque, (4) no rotations, (5) tight contacts, (6) flat curve of Spee.

Primary molar relationships 3

Flush terminal plane (most common) → Class I via late mesial shift/leeway or end-on; mesial step → Class I; distal step → Class II.

Transverse / crossbite 6

Posterior crossbite classified as dental vs skeletal, unilateral vs bilateral, with or without a functional shift.

Treatment-need & outcome indices

IOTN — Dental Health Component 1

Grades treatment NEED 1 (none) → 5 (extreme) using MOCDO (Missing, Overjet, Crossbite, Displacement, Overbite).

Little's irregularity index 1

Sum of the 5 maxillary anterior contact-point displacements (mm); 0 = perfect alignment.

IOTN — Dental Health Component (need)
★ Grade 5 — very greatOJ >9 mm; impeded eruption; cleft; extensive hypodontia
★ Grade 4 — greatOJ 6–9 mm; reverse OJ >3.5 mm; crossbite >2 mm shift; displacement >4 mm; open bite >4 mm
★ Grade 3 — moderate/borderlineOJ 3.5–6 mm (lips apart); reverse OJ 1–3.5 mm; displacement 2–4 mm; open bite 2–4 mm
Grade 2 — littleOJ 3.5–6 mm (lips together); displacement 1–2 mm; deep bite ≥3.5 mm, no trauma
Grade 1 — noneMinor irregularities <1 mm
IOTN — Esthetic Component
★ 10-point photo scale1 = most attractive → 10 = least; 8–10 = definite need
Other indices
★ Little irregularity indexΣ of 5 anterior contact displacements (mm)
PAR (Peer Assessment Rating)Weighted score of occlusal traits; ↓ = improvement (outcome index)
DAI (Dental Aesthetic Index)Regression score combining traits → need cutoffs
ABO Discrepancy Index (DI)Pre-treatment case-difficulty score (board exam)
★ Bolton ratioanterior 77.2% · overall 91.3% (tooth-size)
Angle / Ackerman-Proffitqualitative classifications (above)

Skeletal & dental maturity staging

Cervical vertebral maturation 3

CS1–CS6 staged from C2–C4 on the lateral ceph (no extra radiation). The mandibular growth peak falls between CS3 and CS4.

Cervical vertebral maturation (CVM)
★ CS1 – CS2Before the peak — flat lower borders; growth still ahead
★ CS3 – CS4PEAK in mandibular growth occurs between these stages
★ CS5 – CS6After the peak — growth largely complete
Other maturity indicators
Hand-wrist filmOssification of carpals/sesamoid (more radiation than CVM)
★ Tanner stages (SMR)Sexual maturity 1–5 (puberty)
Dental ageFrom tooth-formation stages (Moorrees-Chadha)
★ Growth-spurt timingGirls ~2 yr earlier than boys

Suture · eruption · resorption staging

Midpalatal suture maturation (Angelieri, CBCT)
★ Stages A–BStraight/scalloped suture — open, expand non-surgically
Stage CTwo parallel lines — borderline (age-dependent)
★ Stages D–EFused (palatine → maxilla) — needs MARPE or SARPE
Primary failure of eruption (PFE) — Table 12.1
★ Type 1All teeth distal to the affected tooth fail to erupt; uniform
Type 2Some eruption but progressively less posteriorly
★ Key pointPFE teeth do NOT respond to orthodontic force (ankylose) — PTH1R gene
Root resorption grading
Grade 0–1None / mild (blunting)
★ Grade 2–3Moderate (≤¼ root) → severe (>⅓ root)

Treatment limits & surgical stability

Envelope of discrepancy

How far teeth can be moved by tooth movement ⊂ growth modification ⊂ surgery — the envelope is asymmetric (more change is possible in some directions). 722

Hierarchy of surgical stability (most → least)
★ Most stableMaxilla up · mandible forward (rigid fixation)
StableMaxilla forward · genioplasty
★ Stable w/ rigid fixation onlyMandible back · maxilla down
★ Least stable / problematicMaxilla down · maxilla wider (transverse)
